node: cut chain replay time by skipping duplicate writes + extending assume-valid
Contributed by Ziyang (as exfer-stack) upstream to ahuman-exfer/exfer, the Exfer chain itself.
This pull request is merged.
https://github.com/ahuman-exfer/exfer/pull/3

## Why

On a 463,031-block chain running on fly.io (4 vCPU, 8 GB,
network-attached volume), replay at startup was the dominant downtime
cost — observed dropping from ~1,100 blocks/s early to **~8 blocks/s
past height 250k**, with CPU pinned and disk-write queue growing.

Forensics identified two defects, both surgical fixes that compose
well with the existing assume-valid plumbing. This PR is **three
atomic commits**, each independently mergeable; commit 3 applies
commit 2's fast path to a sibling call-site I missed on first pass.

---

## A/B benchmark — full replay, both runs to completion

Same `chain.redb` snapshot from fly (height 463,031, fetched via
`fly volumes snapshots create` → temp machine → `fly ssh sftp`).
Two isolated `--datadir` copies, both binaries built from the same
host (NVMe disk, 8 cores). Run sequentially (patched first), then
baseline ran fresh while patched was idle — minimal CPU contention.

### Headline

| | **Baseline (v1.10.1)** | **This PR** | **Speedup** |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| **Total replay wall-clock** | 14,648 s (4.07 h) | 12,319 s (3.42 h) | **1.19×** |
| 0 → 302,400 (assume-valid) | 1,588 s | **16 s** | **99×** |
| 302,400 → 463,031 (full validation) | 13,060 s | 12,303 s | 1.06× |

### Correctness gate

Both runs produced byte-identical final state:

```
Baseline: Replayed 463031 blocks, UTXO set has 360935 entries, SMT: 1171250 nodes + 360935 leaves
Patched:  Replayed 463031 blocks, UTXO set has 360935 entries, SMT: 1171250 nodes + 360935 leaves
```

In addition to this end-to-end parity, the per-block state-root check
(`src/main.rs:3036-3043`) is preserved in both paths and ran on every
single block of the patched run. If
`apply_block_transactions_assume_valid` had a single misapplication
bug, the SMT root would diverge from the on-disk header value and
replay would abort with `state root mismatch at height N`. It does
not, at any of the 302,400 blocks below the checkpoint.

### Why 99× below the checkpoint but ~1× above on local NVMe

- **Below `ASSUME_VALID_HEIGHT`**: Phase 2 skips Ed25519 signature
  verification on every transaction input. Forensics confirmed sig
  verify dominates per-block CPU cost — eliminating it produces the
  ~99× win. (1,588 s → 16 s; ~200 b/s → ~18,000 b/s.)
- **Above `ASSUME_VALID_HEIGHT`**: Phase 2 is intentionally inactive;
  blocks fall back to the full validated path. Phase 1's only
  contribution here is eliminating the 2 duplicate redb write
  transactions per block. On local NVMe this is essentially
  invisible (1.06× ratio); on network-attached storage (fly volumes)
  it was a significant fraction of per-block wall time and the
  reason this work was triggered. The ~8 blocks/s observed on fly
  was a combination of full validation **plus** the duplicate-write
  fsync overhead — Phase 1 removes the latter. We've been operating
  the patched build on fly since the bench finished and it's
  comfortably above 8 b/s in the same height range.
